findings.passage: One of the most effective and straightforward tools at our disposal to attempt to protect the integrity of our elections is requiring the use of photo identification to vote.
findings.note: From her opinion column urging a yes vote on the April 1, 2025 photo ID constitutional amendment. The column is a JPEG; the text was read from the image. She supports requiring photo ID to vote and calls it a tool for election integrity.

findings.passage: Furthermore, qualified electors who do not have photo identification on Election Day would be able to cast a provisional ballot.
findings.note: In the same column, she describes what happens to a voter without photo ID under the amendment: a provisional ballot. She also says military and overseas voters could still use absentee ballots.
subjects: voter with no ID and provisional ballot

findings.passage: For these reasons and more, I advise you to vote YES for voter identification on April 1st and enshrine this integral piece of election integrity in our state constitution.
findings.note: Closing line of the column: she asks readers to vote yes on putting the photo ID requirement in the state constitution.

findings.passage: This amendment language has been approved by the state legislature in two consecutive legislative sessions and would require photo identification when voting. Please take a look and vote YES for voter identification on or before April 1st.
findings.note: March 2025 e-newsletter to constituents, sent with a copy of her column. She asks readers to vote yes on the photo ID amendment.
